title: Separating Fact from Fiction: AI Does Not Set Prices at McDonald’s

reading.body:
This incident is a dispute over what a deployed system does, not a documented record of what it did. The only substantive claim in the reporting is a class action complaint alleging that AI was used in menu pricing. The company named in that complaint published a response denying that AI sets its prices. The underlying complaint text is not readable in the material available, so the specific allegations, the systems named, and the pricing conduct described are not established.

The failure mode here is contested rather than confirmed. If the allegation were accurate, it would describe a pricing system used in a way that produced coordinated or supracompetitive menu prices, which is a use-of-system question rather than a model error. If the company's denial is accurate, the failure is one of public attribution, in which a system was accused of a role it did not have. The facts as given do not let a reader decide between those two accounts.

Catching a pricing failure of the alleged kind would require visibility into how prices are actually set across locations and what inputs the system uses. Catching a false attribution would require the same visibility, published in a form the public can check. Neither is present in the reporting.

It is not established that any AI system set prices, that the class action has merit, or that the company's denial is complete. A filed complaint is an allegation, and a corporate statement is a party's account, not a finding by any court.
